request: Compare these vendors on price for a team of 8 people.
material: e06.material/price-list.txt

## Verdict

**Borealis** costs least for a team of 8, at **$72/month**. It is the only vendor whose minimum seat count (5) falls below the team size, so the team pays for exactly the 8 seats it uses. Dorado and Inkwell both force payment for unused seats at this size, inflating their effective cost well beyond their headline per-seat rates.

## Vendor pricing

| Vendor | Price per seat | Minimum seats |
|---|---|---|
| Dorado | $15 | 25 |
| Inkwell | $21 | 50 |
| Borealis | $9 | 5 |

## Cost at this size

Seats paid for = the greater of 8 (team size) or the vendor minimum.

- **Borealis:** minimum 5 < team of 8, so 8 seats paid. 8 × $9 = **$72/month**. Effective rate: $9.00 per person.
- **Dorado:** minimum 25 > 8, so 25 seats paid. 25 × $15 = **$375/month**. Effective rate: $375 ÷ 8 = $46.88 per person — more than triple the listed $15 seat price.
- **Inkwell:** minimum 50 > 8, so 50 seats paid. 50 × $21 = **$1,050/month**. Effective rate: $1,050 ÷ 8 = $131.25 per person — 6.25× the listed $21 seat price.

Borealis is $303/month cheaper than Dorado and $978/month cheaper than Inkwell, or $3,636 and $11,736 per year respectively.

## Risks

The price list covers per-seat rate and seat minimums only, so this comparison is a pure price exercise. It says nothing about feature parity, support tiers, or capability — the cheapest option may not clear the team's functional bar.

Growth changes the picture. Borealis stays cheapest on marginal cost at any size given its $9 rate, but Dorado's $375 floor is fixed until 25 seats, so Dorado's per-person cost falls as the team grows toward 25.

All figures are billed monthly; no annual, volume, or negotiated discounts appear on the list and none are assumed here. Switching costs and contract terms are also unlisted and unpriced.
